intro_html: An employee moves — a new department, job title, office, manager or company. This turns that into a small record: approved before it happens, dated for the day it takes effect, and applied without ever typing over the employee's history.

features.title: A Move Becomes A Record
features.desc: One record per move, with its own reference, an effective date, a reason and a chatter trail — instead of an edit nobody can trace.

features.title: Five Things Can Change
features.desc: Department, job position, work location, manager, company — any combination. A field left empty means "no change", and nothing else moves.

features.title: Dated History, Not Overwriting
features.desc: Applying writes a new dated version on the employee. The old values stay readable, so "when did she move to Support?" has an answer.

features.title: Approval Enforced In The Code
features.desc: Only an HR Manager can approve, and the check sits inside the method — a script or an API call is refused exactly like the button is.

features.title: Applied On The Day, By Itself
features.desc: A daily scheduled run applies approved transfers when their date arrives. Before that the form says so, instead of offering a button that would be wrong.

features.title: Final Once Applied
features.desc: The employee, the date, the status and every target lock. Reversing a move means recording another one, and the error message says exactly that.

features.title: The "From" Values Stay Frozen
features.desc: The before-values are captured at the moment of applying, so a later change to the employee never rewrites what the record says the person moved from.

features.title: Cross-Company Without A Second Record
features.desc: A move between group companies keeps one employee, one time-off balance, one service history — and only an approver who holds both companies can approve it.

limitations: Applying is final. There is no un-apply, no reset to draft and no undo: reversing a move means recording another transfer back to the previous values.

Manager and company are not dated history. Odoo versions department, job position and work location; a change of manager or company overwrites the current value on the employee, so the module cannot answer who someone's manager was last August.
No back-dating. The effective date must be later than the employee's most recent version, so a move cannot be inserted between two existing ones.
No pay or contract changes. Wage, contract type and working schedule are carried over unchanged; a promotion with a raise needs the salary handled separately.
No bulk transfers. One record per employee — re-organising a twenty-person department means twenty transfers.
No org-chart preview, and no check that a change of manager does not create a reporting loop.
No transfer letter, PDF or email to the employee. The only notification is an internal to-do activity for HR Managers when a transfer is sent for approval.
No cross-company handshake. A move between companies is one approval by one manager who holds both; there is no acceptance step by the receiving company.
A single approval step — no second approver, no delegation, no approval matrix and no escalation if the activity is ignored.
The scheduled run happens once a day, so a transfer effective today may only become applied hours into the day unless someone presses Apply now.
